title: old timers (feat. Nieman)

poetryFrame.leftVertical: THE QUIET WEIGHT OF YEARS TO COME, A PATIENCE BORN FROM MEMORY AND LIGHT
poetryFrame.rightVertical: A CONTINUUM OF LOVED MOMENTS, WHERE TIME SLOWLY LEARNS TO REST
poetryFrame.bottomLine: WAITING FOR THE SIMPLE GLOW OF DAYS UNFORESEEN
sonnetLines: The decades turn like pages turning slow,
A gentle hum where old dreams softly glow.
We trace the lines etched deep upon the face,
Finding comfort in a familiar space.
No rockets fly, no screens command the view,
Just steady skies and morning's misty dew.
The cup is warm, the ritual remains true,
A quiet promise shared between me and you.
Let the years settle like dust on the sill,
To slow the rush of life against our will.
We watch the world drift by in shades of gray,
And let the hurried moments slip away.
Just rocking gently where we used to stand,
The perfect peace held softly in your hand.

lyrics.text: I wonder what will be on TV
In the year 2063
Who will be topping the Billboard charts
And will we all have flying cars
Will there still be global warming
Or will we have heeded their warnings
I hope we'll still see all the mountains and trees
And the cool of the morning breeze
I can't wait to be old timers
We'll sit at our favorite diner
I'll order my coffee and I'll get my tea
Like how it used to be
I can't wait to be old timers
We'll sit on the porch in our rockers
And watch as the neighbors go on with their lives
As I reminisce about mine
I wonder if you'll still be with me
With your wrinkles and wobbly knees
We promised each other 'til death do us part
You better stay right where you are
I can't wait to be old timers
We'll sit at our favorite diner
I'll order my coffee and I'll get my tea
Like how it used to be
I can't wait to be old timers
We'll sit on the porch in our rockers
And watch as the neighbors go on with their lives
As I reminisce about mine
I wonder where you and I will be
In the year 2063
